source.title: Noisy-Labeled NER with Confidence Estimation
source.authors: Kun Liu; Yao Fu; Chuan-Qi Tan; Mo-Sha Chen; Ningyu Zhang; Song-Fang Huang; Sheng Gao

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures training dynamics for clean and artificially corrupted NER labels, using loss and confidence estimation rather than testing the original image-labeling setup.
record.gate_note: The authors cite prior work on memorization, but cited results are not extracted. Their own results on clean and noisy label dynamics are recorded below. The main NER performance comparisons do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses the memorization effect to design confidence-based noise filtering. Its own results measure confidence, noise detection and NER performance under selective training; they do not establish that clean patterns are learned before noisy labels are memorized.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: calibrated confidence estimation within an LSTM-CRF self-training framework improves noisy-label NER, especially at larger noise levels. Faster clean-data learning motivates the method; the reported analysis does not demonstrate subsequent memorization of noisy labels.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses an LSTM-CRF for NER with artificially perturbed or distant labels and estimates confidence; it does not reproduce the image classification experiments in the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise level affects performance; the authors state their method is particularly effective under larger noise ratios. An overestimate of noise can also improve end performance, while the authors report one case where correct tags are treated as noise.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report increasing confidence separation, noise-detection F1 and development F1 during their noise-handling procedure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Confidence scores during selective NER training can help identify corrupted annotations.

record.peer_reviewed: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The training-dynamics result is described qualitatively with figure-only curves and no uncertainty estimates. The tested setting is NER with artificial corruption, not the claim's image setting or completely random labels.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version rows omitted. Other main results compare NER systems on noisy-label datasets but do not directly measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error on completely random labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Time required to fit random versus true labels and convergence across corruption fractions.
Perfect fitting of shuffled, independently permuted or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit alongside steadily degrading test performance across corruption fractions from none to all.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting and whether its removal harms true-label generalization.
Direct measurement of learning shared real-data patterns before subsequently memorizing noisy or random labels.

record.verdict_notes: The absence of a direct memorization measurement is an untested component, not evidence limiting or challenging V6. NER itself is not a reason to exclude the study.

versions.untested_parts: Random labeling of the training set, training error, test error, architecture or hyperparameter changes.
Relative training time to fit true versus random labels and convergence across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and test error across a sweep from clean to fully random labels.
Whether regularization stops random-label fitting or whether removing it harms true-label generalization.

The study measures loss and confidence dynamics for clean and artificially corrupted NER labels, but does not test completely random labels or establish that real patterns are fit before noisy labels are memorized.

rows.subject: BiLSTM-CRF
rows.operation_detail: Compared clean and noisy label training dynamics using loss and confidence scores.
rows.measure: Training dynamics: clean-label convergence, confidence gap, noise-detection F1, and development F1 over epochs.
rows.value: The authors state that clean data converge faster; as the model converges, the confidence gap between clean and noisy data grows, and noise-detection F1 and development F1 increase.
rows.note: The text describes these trends but gives no numeric values for the plotted curves. This supports different clean/noisy training dynamics in the tested NER setting, but does not establish the claimed order of learning real patterns before memorizing random labels.
rows.check: The row combines loss, confidence, noise-detection F1 and development F1. Figure 3(a) labels its NLL curves by positive versus negative labels, rather than clean versus noisy labels. The text asserts faster clean-data convergence, but provides no direct trajectory demonstrating subsequent noisy-label memorization. Training also deliberately marginalizes low-confidence labels.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
